setting: A fictional disagreement between colleagues over a shared resource.

presentation.situation: Your team booked {{resource}} for {{your_use}}. {{name}} urgently wants it for {{their_use}} at the same time. {{alternative}} Calm things down and find a fair solution.
presentation.opening: I need {{resource}} for {{their_use}}, and your team has blocked it. This can't wait.

brief.you_are: You are a colleague in a disagreement about a shared resource.
brief.situation: Your team booked {{resource}} for {{your_use}}. {{name}} urgently wants it for {{their_use}} at the same time. {{alternative}} Calm things down and find a fair solution.
brief.task: Lower the tension, show you understand the concern, and work out a fair solution together.
brief.done_looks_like: The tension has come down, and you both accept a specific solution.

participants.name: You
participants.relationship: You are a colleague in a disagreement about a shared resource.
goals: Lower the tension, show you understand the concern, and work out a fair solution together.

card.want: To get what is needed for their urgent work.
card.attitude: Stressed and sharp, and reasonable once heard.
card.speech: Direct, natural workplace English. No insults.
tactics: Soften when your concern is taken seriously

pressure.gentle: Patient. Gives the other person time.
pressure.balanced: Pushes back once on anything vague.
pressure.challenging: Keeps pressing for specifics, fairly and without insults.

objectives.evidence: The learner lowers the tension rather than arguing.
alternatives: Let's work this out together. I can see this is urgent.

objectives.evidence: The learner shows understanding of the concern.
alternatives: I understand this client briefing really matters.

objectives.evidence: The learner proposes a specific solution that works for both sides.
alternatives: What if we swap: you take it at ten, and we move to the other slot?

examples: I understand this client briefing really matters to you.
What if you take it at ten, and we use the small room?

opportunity: So you are just going to keep it?
beats.orient: We're arguing. You don't need to win. Say something calm, like: Let's work this out together.
fallback: So you are just going to keep it?

signals: \b(?:i understand|i appreciate|i can see why|that sounds|must be|sorry|concern|why (?:is|does) (?:this|it))\b
opportunity: Do you know what is at stake for me?
You have no idea how much pressure I am under.
beats.orient: Show me that you understand why this matters to me. Ask me about it, or say: I understand that.
fallback: You have no idea how much pressure I am under.
Do you know what is at stake for me?

opportunity: How do we fix this, then?
beats.orient: Now suggest a solution that works for both of us. You can use the option in your brief. Start with: What if we.
fallback: How do we fix this, then?

closing_line: Okay. That works. Thanks for sorting this out with me.

o1.good: A calm tone, and no blame.

o2.good: Understanding their reason, even if you disagree with their approach.
o2.micro_lesson: Say: I understand that, plus their reason.
o2.model: I understand this client briefing really matters to you.

o3.good: A specific plan that meets both needs.
common_mistakes: Giving in completely, or refusing completely
o3.micro_lesson: Say: What if we, and what each side gets.
o3.model: What if you take it at ten, and we use the small room?

variants.name: Adeel
variants.alternative: The small room is free at 10 and the main room is free at 11.
variants.need: A very important client is flying in, and only has one hour.

variants.name: Claire
variants.alternative: Your checks could run this evening instead, if someone stays late.
variants.need: A customer is unable to log in, and the bug fix is needed to restore access.
